subject: health
title: Correction and reflection: supportive peer boundaries
essentialQuestion: How can understanding mental and emotional health skills help us explain, decide, create, or solve something that matters?
materials: unit-specific source, model, manipulatives, safe materials, or approved digital tool
keyPoints: A supportive peer listens without promising secrecy, avoids acting as a counselor, and brings in a trusted adult when safety or ongoing care is involved.
A safe communication plan states the limit clearly, recognizes pressure or danger, identifies an exit, and brings in adult or professional support when direct engagement is unsafe.
For supportive peer boundaries, a strong response distinguishes fact from assumption, uses a fictional or public case, and includes a safe next step or appropriate source of support.
privacySafeScenario: Respond to fictional scenarios with coping, support, and escalation choices while protecting privacy.
studentTask: Annotate a supplied fictional exchange about supportive peer boundaries: underline the stated limit, circle any pressure or respectful check-in, and write a two-sentence response that states a boundary plus a safe next step. Add when a trusted adult should enter the plan.
knowledgeCheck: In two or three sentences, explain the most important distinction in supportive peer boundaries; use one lesson fact and name the evidence, safety check, or support route that makes the explanation dependable.
completionCriteria: The response completes every named part of the supportive peer boundaries task using the supplied fictional or public case.
The response uses at least two accurate details from the lesson instruction and distinguishes evidence from assumption.
The response gives a safe, feasible next step or support route and does not depend on private disclosure, body comparison, or recorded media proof.
